instructions.question: What sentiment does the author of this German tweet express: positive, neutral or negative?
instructions.rule: Judge the author's own expressed feeling, not the topic. News, including deaths, accidents and crime, plus ads, results, fan requests and political commentary or accusations are neutral, unless the author adds emotional words, insults, sad emoticons or alarm wording ('Alarmierende', 'Furchterregend'). Laughing, winking or heart cues make jokes, teasing, mild gripes and excited surprise positive, but do not soften stated pain, heartbreak or refusal. Bewilderment at something odd (o_O, wut, ?!?!), dry sarcasm ('Danke.', 'Aha!'), curt rejections, threats and the author's bad state are negative.

neutral.what: News of any topic (deaths, crime, economy), political commentary and accusations, sports results, ads, questions, likes, fan requests, mild everyday remarks and absurd jokes.
examples: #opblitzkrieg Innenminister Pistorius täuscht Interesse an Datensicherheit vor! http #GAGA (Interior minister Pistorius feigns interest in data security!)
Selbstmord: US-Schauspieler Lee Thompson Young ist tot - Kultur | STERN.DE Mobile http (Suicide: US actor Lee Thompson Young is dead)
Müdigkeit frisst Motivation #montag (tiredness eats motivation #monday)
Guten Morgen! Wir wollen euch noch erzählen, was #Apple gestern in Sachen #iPhone erzählt hat: http (Good morning! We want to tell you what Apple said yesterday about the iPhone)
neutral.cues: headline plus link, RT of news, prices, Verkaufe (selling), +1, bitte spielt (please play), open questions, hashtags of political campaigns
neutral.not_for: Headlines with alarm wording, e.g. 'Alarmierende Studie' (alarming study), or the author's 'Unfassbar!' (unbelievable!) are negative.

positive.what: Joy, praise, thanks, stand-alone greetings, welcomes, affection, excitement or delighted surprise, pride in success, and jokes or teasing softened by laughing, winking or heart emoticons.
examples: SIEG!!!!!!!! Chemie gewinnt 2-0 gegen Osnabrück :-D #liga3 (VICTORY!!! Chemie wins 2-0 against Osnabrück)
So unfassbar müde - gute Nacht, ihr Hübschen <3 (so incredibly tired - good night, you lovely people <3)
Schäm dich einfach :P (just be ashamed of yourself :P)
positive.cues: :) / ;) / :D / :P / xD / haha / <3, Gruß (regards), willkommen (welcome), Glückwunsch (congratulations), danke (thanks), genial (brilliant)
positive.not_for: A smiley after heartbreak or refusal, e.g. 'Herz wieder in tausend Stücke zerfallen. Danke. (:' (heart shattered again. Thanks. (:), is negative. Ads and reported wins are neutral.

negative.what: Complaints, anger, disgust, sadness, insults, threats, dry sarcasm, bewilderment at something odd, curt rejections, the author's bad state, alarm-worded news.
examples: Och ne, jetzt singt Nicole auch noch? HILFE. #sg (Oh no, now Nicole is singing too? HELP.)
Einmal Weltuntergang zum Mitnehmen bitten. Danke. (One apocalypse to go, please. Thanks.)
Welches Geschenk hast du zuletzt bekommen? — Eine Bettdecke o.O http (What gift did you get last? — A duvet o.O)
negative.cues: :( / :/ / ;-; / T_T / o_O / wut / ?!?!, scheiße (shit), nervig (annoying), Mist (damn), merkwürdig (weird), einsam (lonely), Aha!, pssst, alarmierend (alarming)
negative.not_for: Plain reports or third-party criticism, e.g. 'Forrester-Analyst übt scharfe Kritik' (analyst sharply criticizes), stay neutral. Teasing with ;) or haha is positive.
